question: What is the estimated monthly per capita household consumption expenditure in rural India, as reported by Household Consumption Expenditure Survey: 2023-24?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹4,122**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The estimated monthly per capita household consumption expenditure in rural India is **₹4,122**, as per the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey: 2023-24.
 
• This survey is conducted periodically by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• It measures consumption expenditure patterns to assess the **standard of living** and economic well-being of households.
 
• The data serves as a basis for calculating important economic indicators, including the **Poverty Line** and Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• Rural consumption expenditure reflects household spending on essentials like food, housing, clothing, healthcare, education, and other goods and services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES)**

 
 
• It is a nationwide survey conducted every five years to collect data on household expenditure.
 
• The survey provides insights into the consumption habits of households across **rural and urban areas**.
 
• Key parameters include food items, non-food items, durable goods, and services.
 
• HCES data is used to estimate poverty levels, inequality, and **budgetary policies**.
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Household Expenditure**
 
 
• This metric is derived by dividing the total household expenditure by the number of members in the household.
 
• It is an important indicator of the **standard of living** and purchasing power of individuals.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Rural and Urban Consumption**
 
 
• Rural consumption is typically focused on necessities like food and basic services.
 
• Urban households spend more on discretionary items such as entertainment, electronics, and luxury goods.
 
 
 
• **Use of HCES Data**
 
 
• Data is used to design and evaluate government welfare programs like the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**.
 
• It helps in identifying **vulnerable groups** and framing poverty alleviation policies.
 
• It is crucial for economic planning and measuring inequality through indicators like the Gini coefficient.
